subject: DPA: Incident notification, evidence access scope, and subprocessor treatment
messages:
From: security@finservco.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@finservco.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Possible data exfiltration — request for DPA notification & evidence scope

Hi Mateo,

We detected anomalous outbound traffic from our integration with Redwood last night that suggests a potential exfiltration of a small set of customer identifiers. We are opening a formal security incident on our end and need to coordinate per the DPA incident notification clauses.

Immediate asks:
- Please confirm within 24 hours whether Redwood considers this a security incident under Section 5 of the DPA and whether you have active logs/forensics covering the time window 2027-09-30 22:00–2027-10-01 02:00 UTC.
- Provide a high-level scope of data potentially exposed (types, approximate row counts). We understand you may need to redact customer-identifiable fields.
- Advise whether any subprocessors were involved in storing or transmitting the affected objects and whether cross-border transfer restrictions apply.

We are asking for evidence handover to support our regulator notification window. We expect initial confirmation first and then a short list of deliverables (redacted logs, chain of custody statements, subprocessor contact points).

Attaching: finserv_initial_incident_report.pdf (internal detection summary).

Regards,
Alex Lee
Head of Security Operations
FinServCo
security@finservco.com

Subject: Re: Possible data exfiltration — request for DPA notification & evidence scope

Alex / FinServCo team,

Thanks for the heads up and the report. I understand the urgency. Initial triage from our side indicates no broad customer plaintext dump — most likely an access pattern anomaly tied to an improperly scoped cache snapshot used by a legacy analytics job.

To be clear on next steps from Redwood:
1) We will confirm within 24 hours whether this meets our incident threshold under Section 5 (we expect to confirm formally within the window you requested).
2) We can produce redacted request logs (request IDs, timestamps, source IPs) and a summary of the model KV cache keys that were accessed. We cannot provide raw customer payloads in the logs without a legal basis; we propose a redacted CSV that masks PII.
3) On subprocessors: the object store involved is a third-party CDN/Storage provider (ClearData) — their involvement is listed in our DPA Appendix B. We will coordinate direct subprocessor evidence requests but will need a signed data request and the legal contact.

Quick asks for you so we can scope delivery:
- Confirm which of your regulatory timelines are controlling (72-hour regulator notify vs. 30-day contractual evidence window).
- Provide preferred contact for legal evidence transfer and whether an encrypted SFTP transfer or DocuSign-stamped chain-of-custody is preferred.

I am looping in Marissa (Legal) and Grace (Customer Success/Account lead) to align on contractual commitments and customer communications.

Thanks,

--
Mateo Alvarez
Account Security Lead
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2027 08:57:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Possible data exfiltration — request for DPA notification & evidence scope

Alex / team,

Following up with legal position and proposed redlines to the DPA language around incident notification and evidence access. Attached is our suggested edit which attempts to balance regulator timelines and our obligations to subprocessors.

High-level points:
- Notification timing: we will confirm incidents to customers and partners within 48 hours of detection and provide an initial factsheet; we cannot commit to substantive forensic exports within 72 hours in all cases because evidence collection may require subprocessor coordination and lawful process. We propose the DPA include a 72-hour "initial notice" obligation and a 14-day forensic evidence delivery window for redacted logs, with an acknowledgement that full raw evidence may require longer and a separate lawful request.
- Subprocessor coordination: Redwood will act as the central coordinator for all subprocessor evidence requests. We require a signed written request (email acceptable) from FinServCo legal with the minimum scope; Redwood will forward to the subprocessor and provide status updates every 72 hours.
- Cross-border transfer: where evidence includes EU customer data, transfers to US-based subprocessors will be handled under SCCs or equivalent safeguards; we will not export raw PII outside the EU without a lawful basis or a court/regulatory order.

Attachments: redline_proposal_dpa_20271002.docx (proposed edits), requested_evidence_checklist.pdf (what we can provide quickly).

Operational suggestion: schedule a 30-min triage call Monday to align on the checklist and evidence handover method.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: security@finservco.com
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Possible data exfiltration — request for DPA notification & evidence scope

Marissa / Mateo,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. FinServCo legal accepts the proposed two-stage approach (initial 72-hour notice, 14-day redacted-forensic deliverable) provided that:
- The initial notice includes a fielded summary of impacted data categories and whether customer-identifiers are in scope;
- Redwood confirms the named subprocessor (ClearData) will engage within 48 hours of a signed request and provide a timeline for raw export availability;
- If ClearData declines or cannot meet regulatory windows, Redwood will provide a written escalation path and a mitigation plan.

We are ok to proceed with the 30-min triage call. Proposed times: Tue 2027-10-05 09:00–09:30 PT or 14:00–14:30 PT. Please confirm.

Attachments: none in this reply — we will sign the minimal written request after the call.

Best,
